messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - hosted-runtime pod-17 reporting sustained memory pressure on KV index + continuous-batching. Potential OOM if not remediated. Auto-escalation to on-call.

sara-oncall: ack, I'm on it. Pulling pod logs and metrics now.

josh-sre: seeing steady growth in kv_index_mem for sessions with very long context (>120k tokens). continuous-batching spike aligns with a rollout 30m ago (batch_window_ms=120 -> 400).

maria-eng: ugh that batch window increase was to improve throughput for embeddings. Can we temporarily revert?

sara-oncall: doing a quick revert to previous batch window on the hosted pool. Command: `rbctl apply --patch batch_window_ms=120 --pool hosted-gpu-a`

incident-bot: action logged: rollback batch_window to 120ms (initiated by sara-oncall). Estimated apply time 45s.

josh-sre: logs: `kv_index.size=1.2GB -> 3.8GB` over 12m for a small subset of sessions. Eviction not keeping up due to long-lived KV entries from huge prefix keys.

dmitri-ml: hypothesis: a customer test is sending repeated long context (system+history) causing continuous batching to merge requests and inflate KV caches. Recommend rate-limiting or hard cap on prefix length at the LB.

lia-support: flagged top 3 customers with heavy long-context usage to account team. No customer-visible errors yet but degraded tail latency. Need comms ready if OOM escalates.

josh-sre: mitigation plan: 1) rollback batch_window (in flight). 2) set emergency eviction multiplier to 2.0 on pool. 3) apply session_context_token_cap=10000 for hosted-gpu-a (soft reject + 429). I'll run 2 and 3 after rollback completes.

sara-oncall: rollback completed. Monitoring memory.

incident-bot: status update: rollback succeeded at +70s.

josh-sre: applying eviction multiplier now: `rbctl set --pool hosted-gpu-a eviction.multiplier=2.0`

dmitri-ml: also push a quick runtime hotpatch to disable cross-session KV merge for the next 15m: `GC_DISABLE_KV_MERGE=true` (will prevent batch-level kv coalescing).

maria-eng: hotpatch applied to 50% of pods in pool for canary. No regressions so far.

lia-support: created short customer note draft: "We're investigating elevated latency for long-context workloads; engineering applied throttles and rollbacks to reduce impact." Request approval to send if tail latency continues.

sara-oncall: memory stabilizing, kv_index trending down from 3.8GB -> 1.4GB over 10m. Keep throttles in place and continue to monitor 30m.

josh-sre: follow-ups: schedule postmortem, add pre-merge test that simulates large prefix sequences + batching, and gate batch_window increases behind a canary that monitors kv_index growth.

dmitri-ml: will prepare a model-aware suggestion: auto-reduce batch_window for sessions flagged as long-context. Could avoid full rollback next time.

lia-support: holding off on external comms for now. If we see any customer 5xx we'll send update with mitigation steps.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (rollback, eviction bump, kv-merge disable). Memory pressure reduced. No customer-facing outages detected. Assigned: postmortem -> sara-oncall, eng analysis -> dmitri-ml + josh-sre, comms -> lia-support.

sara-oncall: closing pager for now; will keep monitoring and open a follow-up thread for the postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
